question: Which Indian Union Territory has the most Scheduled Castes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Delhi has the highest population of Scheduled Castes among Union Territories in India, as per census data.
 
• The Scheduled Castes population in Delhi is concentrated in areas like Najafgarh, Karol Bagh, and other regions with significant urban settlements.
 
• Scheduled Castes in Delhi include various communities such as Chamars, Valmikis, and others identified under the SC category.
 
• The urbanization of Delhi has led to higher employment opportunities for Scheduled Castes in sectors like construction, sanitation, and labor-intensive industries.
 
• Government schemes like Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP) are actively implemented in Delhi to uplift the socio-economic conditions of SC communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Castes (SCs)**

 
 
• Scheduled Castes are officially designated groups of historically disadvantaged people recognized in the Constitution of India.
 
• They are provided with reservations in education, employment, and political representation under Articles 341 and 342 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Census Data**
 
 
• The Census of India collects detailed population data about Scheduled Castes and other communities.
 
• It provides insights into demographic distribution, literacy rates, and socio-economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP)**
 
 
• SCSP is a targeted development program aimed at improving the socio-economic conditions of Scheduled Castes.
 
• It ensures adequate budgetary allocations for SC-specific schemes across sectors.
 
 
 
• **Urbanization and SCs**
 
 
• Urbanization has led to increased participation of Scheduled Castes in non-agricultural sectors such as construction and services.
 
• However, challenges like discrimination and social exclusion persist despite economic opportunities.
